transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, hello Doctor. Thank you for fitting me in, I really appreciate it. I hope I'm not wasting your time. 

Um... I guess I'm here because I've been having a bit of a rough patch. Nothing I can't handle usually, but... well, I started having these thoughts lately. Just... thinking that maybe my family might be better off if I just didn't wake up in the morning. It's probably just stress, you know? But it... it kind of scared me. Scared me enough that I actually blurted it out to my supervisor at work, and he told me I should come talk to someone. 

I'm sorry to drop that on you right away. Is that... is that the sort of thing you can help with? I just want to make sure I'm in the right place.
How long have you been having these thoughts about your family being better off without you?

Well, um... I guess it hasn't been that long, really. Maybe just about two weeks? It sort of started around the time my daughter left Georgia to join the military. I'm so proud of her, of course, but... well, the house just feels a little empty, and I think I just let myself get a bit too down about it. This whole change in me, it's just been since she left. That's not too unusual, right? Lots of parents get a little sad when their kids leave home, don't they? I'm sure I'm just overreacting a bit.
Have you been enjoying things you normally like to do since your daughter left for the military?

Well, I suppose I haven't been doing quite as much of my usual stuff. I mean, I'm sure I'll get back to it soon enough. But, you know, I usually love messing with my tomato plants out back, or... or sanding down some wood at my workbench. I usually catch the Falcons games, too, and I always stay after church to chat with folks. 

But lately... I don't know, it's silly, really. I just kind of look at all those things and it feels like... like they belong to somebody else. I just haven't had the drive for it. I'm sure it's just a phase, though. That makes sense, doesn't it? Just needing a little break from things?
Have you experienced any loss of interest in activities that you normally find pleasurable?

Oh, I'm sorry, did I not explain that right just a minute ago? I want to make sure I'm giving you what you need. 

But, yes, like I was saying about my tomato plants and the workbench... I guess you could say I've lost interest in them. It's just like I mentioned, I haven't really had the spark for any of my usual hobbies lately. I'm sorry if I wasn't clear before. I hope I'm making sense now... is that what you were asking about?
Have you experienced any changes in your appetite or sleep patterns since your daughter left?

Well, um... I guess my appetite has been a little off lately. Nothing to really worry about, I promise! It's just that, well, most days I kind of have to force myself to just eat a few bites. 

Even the meals I normally really look forward to, you know, whether I'm on shift at the warehouse or just sitting at home... it just sort of sits there on the plate until I end up having to throw it out. I feel awful wasting it, I really do. I just haven't had much of a stomach for anything. But that's pretty normal when you're adjusting to a big change like your kid moving away, right? Just a little stress taking away the appetite? I'm sure it'll pass real soon.
Have you experienced any feelings of worthlessness?

Well, I... I wouldn't say worthlessness, exactly. That's a pretty strong word, isn't it? I mean, I know I'm a good worker at the warehouse, and I try to be a good neighbor. 

But... well, since my daughter left, I do catch myself... I keep going over it in my head. I just keep thinking that maybe I failed her somehow. You know? Like, maybe if I'd been a better father, things would have been different, or I would have done something different to help her get set up in life. It's silly, I know. I shouldn't be dwelling on it. I'm sure every parent feels a little guilty when their kid leaves the nest, right? That's just a normal part of letting go, isn't it? I hope I'm not making too big a deal out of it.
Have you had any days where you felt completely unable to carry out your daily activities due to these thoughts and feelings?

Well, um... I guess there have been a few times where things got a little... overwhelming. But I'm sure that's to be expected, right? With everything going on. 

I mean, I don't want you to think I'm slacking off or anything. I've always been a hard worker. But, well, at the warehouse, I made a couple of slip-ups. Just silly mistakes, really, but... I guess they were a bit more serious than I realized. It got to the point where my supervisor actually found me just sitting in my truck before my shift, before the sun even came up. I just couldn't seem to make myself go inside. He ended up getting occupational health involved, which I feel terrible about. I hate causing a fuss for anyone.

And at home... well, I've let a few things slide. Just some bills and chores piling up, things I'd normally take care of right away. It's embarrassing to admit, honestly. I usually keep a very tidy house. I hope you don't think less of me for it... I'm trying my best to get back on track, I really am. Is it normal to struggle this much with just the day-to-day stuff when you're feeling this way?
Have you had any days where you felt completely unable to carry out your daily activities due to these thoughts and feelings for most of the day?

Well, um... I guess I might have repeated myself a little there, I'm sorry. But, yeah, to answer your question... it has been most of the day, on some of those days. 

Like I was saying about the warehouse... I didn't mean to make a big deal out of it, but when my supervisor found me out in my truck before dawn, I... I ended up just sitting out there for hours. I couldn't get myself to walk through the doors for my whole shift. And that's when he called in occupational health. I feel so bad about making them go out of their way for me. I'm usually so reliable, you know? 

And with the stuff at home, the bills and the chores... it's not just that I'm putting them off for an hour or two. Whole days go by where I just... I look at the stack of mail or the dishes, and I just can't seem to make my hands do the work. I just sit there. I know I should be handling my responsibilities like a normal person. It's just... it's been harder lately to get through the day. That makes sense, though, doesn't it? Given how tired I've been feeling? I really am trying to push through it so I don't let anyone down.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or the opposite, feeling restless and unable to sit still?

Well, I... I don't want you to think I'm completely falling apart or anything. I'm usually pretty sharp, and I try to keep a good pace at the warehouse. But, um... a few of the guys at work have been asking if I'm coming down with something. 

They, uh... they said I've been walking a lot slower lately. And I guess sometimes it takes me a minute to answer when they ask me a question. It's just... I don't know, it feels like my body is moving through mud sometimes. Like everything just takes so much more effort than it used to. But I'm sure that's just because I haven't been sleeping well, right? Anybody would be a little sluggish if they were tired. I really try to perk up when they talk to me, I don't want them thinking I'm not pulling my weight. It's okay to have an off week every now and then, isn't it?
How many days a week have you been feeling this way since your daughter left?

Well, um... I guess it's been pretty much every day. But, you know, it hasn't been going on forever. Just... just for about two weeks now. Ever since my daughter left Georgia to join the military. 

I don't want you to think this is how I usually am. I'm normally very steady. It's just... well, seeing her off, it was a big adjustment, you know? I'm so proud of her, of course I am, but the house feels awfully quiet without her around. I'm sure anyone would feel a little thrown off balance for a couple of weeks after something like that, right? It's perfectly normal to need a little time to adjust to a big change like that, isn't it? I just... I don't want you to think this is a permanent thing with me. I'm sure I'll bounce back soon.
Have you had any thoughts of self-harm in addition to thinking your family might be better off without you?

Well, um... I really don't want you to think I'm a danger to myself or anything crazy like that. I would never actually do anything to hurt myself, I promise. It's just... 

Well, I guess the reason I finally agreed to come in is because... sometimes, when things get really quiet and I'm just sitting there, I catch myself thinking that maybe... maybe everyone would just be better off if I didn't wake up in the morning. It's not that I want to die, you know? It's just this passing thought that maybe I'm more of a burden than a help right now. 

But it did scare me a little when the thought kept coming back. That's why I finally mentioned it to my supervisor when he found me in the truck. I figured it was the responsible thing to do, to let someone know. I just didn't want to keep it a secret if it was something I should be worried about. That was the right thing to do, wasn't it? Telling him, I mean? I just want to make sure I'm handling this the right way.
Have you felt that these thoughts of your family being better off without you are something you cannot control?

Well, um... I guess that's the thing. I try really hard to just push them away and focus on work, but... yeah, they do kind of just pop up on their own. That's really why I'm here, honestly. 

I mean, I kept having those thoughts about... you know, them being better off if I just didn't wake up. And it started to scare me that I couldn't just shake it off like I usually do. That's why I finally said something to my supervisor when he checked on me. I didn't want to make a big fuss, but I figured it was better to be safe and get some help, right? I just want to get back to normal so I can be there for my family. That makes sense, doesn't it?
Have you felt that these thoughts and feelings have been interfering with your ability to work or take care of things at home for more than half of the days since your daughter left?

Well, I... I guess so. I mean, I don't want you to think I'm completely falling apart or anything. I'm usually very on top of things. But... yeah, I suppose it's been most days lately. 

At home, I just... I haven't been getting to the mail like I should. Some bills have been sitting there, which isn't like me at all. I usually pay them the day they come in. And at work... well, I guess I have been making a few more mistakes than usual. Nothing I couldn't fix, normally, but... it did get to the point where my supervisor got a bit concerned. That's why he came looking for me that morning when I was just sitting in my truck before my shift. He thought it would be a good idea to get occupational health involved, just to be safe. 

I really am trying my best to keep it all together, though. It's just a temporary slump, right? Anyone would struggle a bit with their focus when they're dealing with a big adjustment like this, don't you think? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right things to get back on track.
Have you felt hopeless about the future for most of the days since your daughter left?

Oh, no, no, I wouldn't say hopeless. I... I really don't want you to think I've just given up or anything like that. I know things are gonna get better once I get through this little rut. 

I mean, I still have my job, and my family needs me, so I know there's a lot to look forward to. I just need to get my focus back, you know? I still firmly believe things will work out fine in the long run. It's just a matter of putting my head down and getting through the rough patch. That's the right way to look at it, isn't it? Just trying to stay positive about what's ahead?
Have you felt that these thoughts and feelings have been present nearly every day since your daughter left?

Well, um... yeah, I guess it has been pretty much every day. But I really don't want to make it sound like it's been going on forever, you know? 

It's really just been... well, about two weeks. Ever since my daughter left Georgia for the military. It's just been this whole change in me since she headed out. I mean, two weeks isn't that long in the grand scheme of things, right? It's perfectly normal to take a couple of weeks to adjust when your kid moves away like that, isn't it? I'm sure I'll be bouncing back any day now.
Have you felt that these thoughts and feelings have been severely impairing your ability to function in daily life?

Severely? Oh, no, I wouldn't use that word at all. I really don't want you to get the wrong idea and think I'm just... you know, helpless or something. I'm still getting up every morning, putting my boots on, and going to work. I'm definitely still functioning. 

Like I mentioned, it's just been a little harder to keep all the plates spinning with the mail and the focus at work, but I'm not incapacitated by any means. I'm still taking care of business the best I can. I mean, as long as I'm still getting up and making the effort every day, that means it's not too serious, doesn't it? I just want to make sure you know I'm still holding my own.
Have your symptoms lasted for less than two weeks or more than two weeks?

Well, like I said before, it's really just been... right around two weeks. Ever since my daughter left Georgia for the military, that's when this whole change in me started. So it hasn't been a long time at all, just about two weeks. That's a pretty normal amount of time to feel a little off after a big change like that, right? I'm sure I'll be back to my old self real soon.
Have you felt that these thoughts and feelings have caused significant distress or impairment in your social, occupational, or other areas of life?

Well, um... I guess it depends on what you mean by significant, you know? I mean, I'm still trying my best. But, I suppose... well, I have let things slip a little bit. 

At home, the mail's just sort of piling up on the counter. Bills and stuff. I usually handle all that right away, but I just haven't had the energy to sort through it. That's not too terrible, though, right? Everyone gets behind on paperwork sometimes. 

But at work... well, I guess it did get a little out of hand. I was making some mistakes, and, um... my supervisor actually found me just sitting out in my truck before my shift one morning. It was before dawn, and I just couldn't get myself to go inside. He got occupational health involved after that. I was really embarrassed about it, to be honest. I don't want them thinking I can't do my job, because I can, I'm just... having a rough couple of weeks. That makes sense, doesn't it? That they'd want to check on me? I'm really trying to get back on track so they don't have to worry anymore.
Would you say that most days, you have had either no pleasure or much less pleasure than usual in most of your activities?

Well, um... I guess you could say that, yeah. But I don't want it to sound like I'm just sitting around moping all day, you know? It's just... well, usually I like to mess with my tomato plants out back, or I'll go sand some wood at my workbench. I usually watch the Falcons games, too, and I always stay after church on Sundays just to talk with folks. 

But lately... I don't know, I just look at all that stuff and it feels like it belongs to somebody else. Like I just can't find the point in getting started on it. I still go to church, of course, I just... head home a little quicker. That's not too unusual for someone going through a tough patch, is it? I mean, it's okay to take a little break from your hobbies sometimes, right? I'm sure I'll get back to my tomatoes soon enough.
